ai_show_review.summary: Rare Rosemary & fiery Dark Star jam with tight rhythm section
ai_show_review.blurb: The set features a scorching Dark Star > Saint Stephen sequence and the only known live rendition of “Rosemary.” The Other One suite and New Potato Caboose highlight Phil’s thunderous bass while Jerry’s guitar soars. Recording quality is good for a ’68 soundboard despite some hiss.
ai_show_review.review:
December 7, 1968 finds the Dead at Bellarmine College delivering one of the most intriguing late‑‘60s performances. The first set kicks off with an interstellar Dark Star that morphs seamlessly into Saint Stephen, showcasing Garcia’s daring volume‑knob experiments and blistering leads. A gritty New Potato Caboose follows, giving Phil Lesh a chance to unleash a nasty, almost classical bass jam before the band dives into a sprawling The Other One suite that feels both intense and exploratory.  
The second set is where the show truly cements its place in the archives: “Rosemary” appears for the first (and only) time live, a quiet but priceless moment, while the closing Morning Dew > And We Bid You Good Night segues cleanly and provides a reflective close. Despite the inevitable hiss and occasional tape glitches typical of 1968 soundboards, the recording captures each instrument with surprising clarity, making this a must‑listen for completists and anyone craving that raw, exploratory energy of the Dead’s early era.

best_recording.reason: Provides the clearest capture of the rare Rosemary and the standout Dark Star jam, with overall good soundboard fidelity despite period hiss.

key_highlights: Rare live performance of “Rosemary” – the only known recording.
Scorching Dark Star > Saint Stephen sequence with blazing guitar work.
Intense The Other One suite and powerful New Potato Caboose bass jam.
Clean Morning Dew > And We Bid You Good Night segment despite overall tape hiss.
song_highlights: And We Bid You Good Night

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers blazing, intergalactic tones on Dark Star and stellar solos throughout; his lead vocals on Rosemary are also praised.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a nasty bass jam on New Potato Caboose and thunderous foundation during The Other One suite, occasionally sounding classical‑like.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums keep the flow steady, supporting the improvisations with solid timing.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann’s drumming adds a tight backbone that underpins the high‑energy jams.
